meta.title: ModelHub — the independent frontier model scoreboard
meta.description: Open ranking of frontier AI models. Third-party numbers, no marketing, with the source and the date in plain sight.

masthead.blurb: Closed and open-source models on the same field. Numbers come from third-party evaluations and human voting; what the vendor claims never counts toward the score.

panel.degradedSource: {source} did not respond on the last run; showing its data from {date}
panel.agingSource: {source} has not published a new snapshot in {days} days (last: {date})

table.agedCategoryTitle: The source behind this category has not published a new snapshot in {days} days
table.provisionalNote: These models have fewer than {min} of {total} categories measured. They stay visible but don't compete for a slot: spreading the weight across only the available categories lifts a thinly measured model on what it is missing, not on being better.
table.awaitingVotesTitle: Has the benchmarks but hasn't accumulated LMArena votes yet. This is not a penalty.

footer.methodNote: The composite weights Reasoning 25 · Coding 25 · Math 20 · Human preference 15 · Instructions 15. Multimodal is measured separately and stays out of the composite: penalising a text-only model for a category it does not compete in would invent a difference that isn't there.
footer.sourceNote: Sources: Epoch AI (CC-BY-4.0), LMArena (CC-BY-4.0) and LiveBench (Apache-2.0). Every run lands as an auditable commit in the repo.
footer.swebenchNote: SWE-bench Verified comes from Epoch's own runs. The agentic scaffold leaderboard at swebench.com is not ingested because its CC-BY-NC licence conflicts with this MIT repo:

compare.title: Compare models
compare.intro: Pick two to four models. The bars share a 0–100 axis, so lengths are directly comparable across categories and across models.
compare.empty: Select at least one model to compare.
compare.tableView: The same numbers, as a table
compare.visionNote: Outside the composite. Measured separately, because a text-only model doesn't compete here.

model.descriptionPending: Description pending. Editorial descriptions are generated by Layer B using a local model and approved by a person before publishing; it hasn't been run for this model yet.
model.partialNote: Partial composite: no measurement for {missing}. The weight is spread across the available categories only, and the model is flagged rather than zero-filled.
model.historyScope: The history available today comes from LMArena, the only source that publishes its full time series. Epoch and LiveBench publish point-in-time snapshots, so their history accumulates run by run from the day the daily ingest started.
model.historyBreaks: The window starts on 2026-01-01, after Arena's most recent methodology change. That is why this line can be drawn continuous without lying: it doesn't cross a break.
model.acquisitionPending: Pending. Acquisition links (HuggingFace repo, provider page, API docs, Ollama tag) are assembled deterministically by Layer B; the fields exist in the schema and stay empty until then.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.intro: Everything here can be reproduced by hand from the public JSON in the repository. If a number on this site disagrees with this page, the site is wrong.

formula.title: The composite, exactly
formula.body: Each benchmark is placed on a 0–100 scale. Within a category the available benchmarks are averaged, and those categories are weighted like this:
formula.inputs_reasoning: GPQA Diamond, SimpleQA Verified (Epoch) · LiveBench Reasoning
formula.inputs_coding: SWE-bench Verified (Epoch) · LiveBench Coding and Agentic Coding
formula.equation: composite = Σ(category score × weight) ÷ Σ(weight of categories with data)
formula.normalisation: Benchmarks already reported as percentages are used as-is. LMArena's Bradley-Terry ratings are not percentages, so they are min-max normalised against the cohort present in each build: in the current build, {min} and {max} are the 0 and the 100. This means a model's normalised Arena value can move even when its rating doesn't, if a model enters or leaves either extreme.
formula.multimodal: Multimodal stays out of the composite and is shown as a separate vision score. Including a category most text models don't compete in would mean penalising them for an absence that says nothing about their quality.

coverage.title: The coverage gate
coverage.body: A model needs data in at least 4 of the 5 categories to enter the main ranking. Below that it appears in the Provisional section: visible, with its composite computed, but without a rank number.
coverage.example: This exists because of a real problem. Since the weight is spread across only the categories that have data, a thinly measured model rises on what it is MISSING rather than on being better. Qwen3-Max-Instruct, with 3 of 5 categories, was landing at rank 5, above models measured on all five. That is precisely the bias this site exists to fight, so it is corrected in code rather than in a footnote.
coverage.newModels: The threshold is 4 and not 5 on purpose. A newly released model can have all four benchmarks and no LMArena votes yet; that case ranks normally, flagged as awaiting human votes. Sufficient evidence is required; being new is not punished.
coverage.current: In the current build: {ranked} ranked models and {provisional} provisional, with the threshold at {min} of 5.

variants.title: Variants of the same model
variants.body: A vendor publishes the same model under several configurations: effort levels, thinking modes. They are the same weights with a different inference budget, so they are grouped under one canonical model. That forces a decision about which value to use when a benchmark arrives more than once, and the decision moves the ranking.
variants.bug: The concrete case: Claude Opus 5 had three variants in LiveBench, and all three entered the Coding category average separately. That benchmark outweighed Epoch 3 to 1, not because it measured better, but because the vendor published more variants. Fixing it changed the top three: GPT-5.6 Sol fell to #3 and Muse Spark 1.1 rose to #2.
variants.tradeoff: We choose a single configuration per model and use it across all of its benchmarks; when a benchmark did not measure that configuration, we leave the gap — and the coverage drops — rather than substituting a different configuration.
variants.principle: This is the same principle applied to SWE-bench scaffolds: reveal the configuration, don't hide it. The mechanisms differ — a scaffold is another system, by another author, contributing much of the result; an effort level is the same weights with a different knob — but the principle is identical, and in both cases it exists for the same reason: to stop a published number from describing a configuration nobody ran.
variants.disclosure: That is why the configuration is never hidden: on each model page, the sources table states exactly which variant produced each number and how many were published.
variants.option_model: choose ONE configuration for the whole model and use it across every benchmark: the effort label with the widest coverage wins, ties going to the variant published without a qualifier. If a benchmark never measured that configuration, the cell is left empty and coverage reflects it. This is the current value.
variants.option_default: use, benchmark by benchmark, the variant published without an effort qualifier; if none exists, fall back to the best. Rejected as the default because it chooses separately per benchmark: a model could take max-effort in Math and xhigh in Coding, a configuration nobody runs.
variants.option_best: use the highest score across variants. It reflects the model's ceiling, but rewards publishing more variants: the maximum of five draws beats the maximum of one.
variants.option_average: average the variants. Rejected as the default: nobody runs 'the mean effort level', so it invents a configuration that does not exist, understating the peak and overstating the cheap variant.
variants.option_separate: do not group; treat each variant as its own model. This is the most consistent with the scaffold rule, but it is not viable today: each source names variants differently (Epoch uses '_max', LiveBench '-max-effort', LMArena '-high'), so without grouping we would hand-maintain an alias table per variant per source. That collides with the zero-daily-maintenance constraint, and it would fragment coverage enough to empty the main ranking. Not implemented.
variants.current: Every affected number states on the model page which configuration was used. Under the current policy the unqualified variant wins most often, followed by xhigh, high and max. When a benchmark never measured the chosen configuration we prefer to leave the gap and lower the coverage rather than substitute another one: a composite with one cell fewer is more honest than one that mixes configurations.

dedup.title: The LMArena duplication guard
dedup.body: LMArena snapshots are sometimes published with several rows per model, carrying different ratings and repeated ranks. Taking them at face value would break the ranking visibly.
dedup.example: A concrete case: the 2026-07-21 snapshot returns 1,113 rows for the overall category spread across only 378 distinct models, with rank 1 appearing three times at three different ratings. The 2026-07-20 snapshot has the same problem. The 2026-06-04 one is clean: 365 rows, 365 models.
dedup.rule: The rule: if rows ÷ distinct models exceeds 1.2, the whole snapshot is rejected and the ingest falls back to the last clean one. It is not 'repaired' by guessing which of the three rows is the real one. The same test is applied to the history, so trajectories don't inherit duplicated snapshots either. Rejections are recorded in data/status.json.

sourceTypes.title: Where a number is allowed to come from
sourceTypes.body: Every score records what kind of source it came from. The distinction is not decorative: it decides whether the number enters the composite.
sourceTypes.human_eval: blind human voting, such as LMArena. Enters the composite.
sourceTypes.third_party_benchmark: an evaluation run by an independent third party, such as Epoch AI or LiveBench. Enters the composite.
sourceTypes.vendor_claim: a figure published by whoever sells the model. Stored and displayed, but NEVER entered into the composite.
sourceTypes.why: A vendor has a direct incentive to pick the setup that flatters it, and there is no way to audit a run it never published. The exclusion is therefore structural rather than a case-by-case judgement: it doesn't depend on whether we happen to trust a given company.

breaks.title: LMArena's methodology breaks
breaks.body: LMArena has changed how its rating is computed three times. Figures either side of a change are not comparable with each other:
breaks.window: Drawing a continuous line across a break would invent a trend that never happened. That is why the history window starts on 2026-01-01, after the most recent break: the plotted series doesn't cross one. Anyone moving that date earlier has to annotate the breaks or cut the series at the last one.

exclusions.title: What was left out, and why
exclusions.swebench: The swebench.com leaderboard is excluded on licensing grounds: its data is CC-BY-NC (non-commercial) and this repository is MIT, which does permit commercial use. Shipping that data here would hand anyone who forks the project a licence promising more rights than they actually have. The SWE-bench Verified figures that are used come from Epoch AI's own CC-BY licensed runs. Beyond the licence there is a technical reason: swebench.com rows describe agent scaffolds rather than bare models, and the scaffold often matters more than the model.
exclusions.others: Also excluded: HuggingFace's Open LLM Leaderboard, whose Space still reports as running while its results dataset hasn't moved since March 2025, and aider's Polyglot leaderboard, frozen since October 2025 even though the project itself is alive. Mixing 2025 figures with 2026 figures in a ranking whose whole premise is currency would be worse than omitting them.

reproduce.title: How to check it yourself
reproduce.body: There is no external database. Everything feeding this page is a versioned text file:
reproduce.git: Every daily run lands as a commit. That means any change to any number is an auditable diff: you can see when it changed, by how much, and which run did it.
